options.motion: Shapes rotating, tiling, morphing into each other, modular patterns shifting in sequence, rhythmic synchronisation to music.
options.use: Brand identities in motion, music visuals, transitions, event loops, logo builds.
options.vs: Bauhaus is a specific historical geometric vocabulary; abstract geometric is general. Generative uses code-driven variation.
options.prompt: Art-direct as abstract geometric motion: compose only with circles, squares, triangles, lines and arcs on a modular grid; 2-4 flat colors with strong contrast; no texture, no gradients; build rhythm through repetition; animate with rotations in 90° steps, shape-to-shape morphs, modular pattern shifts staggered across the grid (stagger from center, 30-60 ms), and synchronize hits to the beat with power4.out 200-400 ms.

options.what: Visuals produced by rules and algorithms (noise fields, recursion, flocking, randomness with seeds) rather than drawn by hand.
options.looks: Flow fields, noise textures, recursive subdivisions, line densities, dot distributions, emergent patterns; palettes often limited and carefully tuned.
options.motion: Continuous evolution: noise-driven drift, growth algorithms, reactive systems, seeded variation; often data- or audio-reactive.
options.use: Brand identity systems, data art, AI and tech brands, installations, event visuals.
options.vs: Particle-based is one generative technique; abstract geometric is often hand-composed. Must be deterministic (seeded) for rendering.
options.prompt: Art-direct as generative: produce visuals with a seeded algorithm in canvas or SVG (flow field, Perlin/simplex noise, recursive subdivision or circle packing); use a fixed seed so renders are deterministic and drive state from timeline time, not Math.random or requestAnimationFrame; tune a limited palette of 3-5 colors on a dark or paper ground; thin 0.5-1.5px strokes or small dots at high density; animate by advancing the noise offset with time and revealing structure progressively.

options.what: Imagery built from thousands of small points that flow, swarm, assemble into forms and disperse.
options.looks: Dense dot clouds, glowing points on dark grounds, trails, dust, sparks, forms emerging from and dissolving into particles.
options.motion: Swarming, attraction and repulsion, particles assembling into a logo or product, dispersing on transitions, flowing along fields.
options.use: Tech and AI brands, data themes, logo reveals, sci-fi, event openers.
options.vs: Generative covers any algorithmic look; particle-based is specifically point systems. Must be seeded for deterministic rendering.
options.prompt: Art-direct as particle-based: render 2,000-20,000 particles on canvas or WebGL with a seeded PRNG; 1-3px points with additive blending on a dark background (#05050A), in 1-2 hues plus white; motion driven by a noise field and target positions sampled from the logo or product silhouette; animate particles assembling into the form (power3.inOut 1500-2500 ms with per-particle delay), holding with slight jitter, then dispersing on transition; compute positions from timeline time for seekable renders.

options.what: Art direction dominated by rich, smooth color gradients (mesh, aurora, radial glows) as the main visual material.
options.looks: Multi-color mesh gradients, aurora glows, grainy gradients, blurred blobs of color, soft transitions, often with white or dark type on top.
options.motion: Slowly flowing and morphing gradients, color shifts, glows pulsing, blobs drifting behind content.
options.use: SaaS and fintech brands, AI products, backgrounds for type-led films, music.
options.vs: Holographic is angle-dependent iridescence on surfaces; gradient-heavy uses gradients as ambient fields. Duotone maps images to two colors.
options.prompt: Art-direct as gradient-heavy: build backgrounds from 3-5 large blurred color blobs (radial-gradients or divs with filter: blur(80-140px)) in harmonious hues, layered into a mesh-gradient feel; add 3-6% film grain on top to prevent banding; keep type crisp in white or near-black with high contrast; animate blobs drifting and morphing slowly (8-15 s sine loops, transforms only), hue shifts of 10-20° over the piece.

options.what: Everything rendered in one hue (or pure grayscale) at varying lightness, relying on value, form and type for hierarchy.
options.looks: Black, white and grays, or tints and shades of one color; strong typographic hierarchy; contrast from value and scale; photography in black and white.
options.motion: Motion carries emphasis that color cannot: scale, position, masking, light and shadow sweeps.
options.use: Premium brands, developer tools, fashion, documentary, serious topics.
options.vs: Duotone uses two colors; monochrome uses one hue. Extreme minimalism is about element count, not color.
options.prompt: Art-direct in monochrome: restrict the palette to a single hue at 5-7 lightness steps (or pure grayscale #000 to #FFF); black-and-white photography; build hierarchy only through value, scale, weight and space; no accent color; animate emphasis with scale, masked reveals and light sweeps (a white-to-transparent gradient moving across) using power3.out 500-700 ms.

options.what: Images and layouts mapped to two colors, typically shadows to one hue and highlights to another.
options.looks: Photos remapped to two contrasting hues (e.g. navy and pink), flat two-color graphics, bold color identity, strong contrast.
options.motion: Duotone photo sequences cutting on beat, color pairs swapping between scenes, gradient-map transitions.
options.use: Music and streaming brands, event promos, campaigns, editorial social content.
options.vs: Monochrome uses one hue; duotone uses two. Risograph often creates duotones but adds grain and overprint.
options.prompt: Art-direct in duotone: map every photograph to two colors (shadows to a dark hue like #1E1A5F, highlights to a bright hue like #FF4F8B) using an SVG feColorMatrix grayscale plus feComponentTransfer table, or CSS grayscale + mix-blend-mode layers; use the same two colors for all graphics and type; allow one pair per scene and swap pairs between scenes on the cut; animate with beat-cut photo sequences and color-pair swaps.

options.what: Restrained, expensive-feeling art direction: space, elegant serifs, rich dark or warm neutral palettes, fine materials and slow motion.
options.looks: Black, deep green, oxblood or cream grounds; gold or champagne accents used sparingly; refined serif or thin wide sans with generous tracking; lots of negative space; macro product photography; fine rules.
options.motion: Slow and weighted: long expo/sine eases (1-2 s), slow push-ins, gentle fades between sequences, light gliding over surfaces; never bouncy.
options.use: Fashion, jewellery, watches, automotive, hospitality, premium tech and finance.
options.vs: Fashion editorial is bold and provocative; luxury is quiet. Extreme minimalism can be cold; luxury adds material richness.
options.prompt: Art-direct as luxury: deep ground (#0B0B0B, #0F2A22 or cream #EFE8DC); one champagne/gold accent (#C8A96A) used on at most one element; refined high-contrast serif or thin wide sans in uppercase with +12-20% tracking, small sizes; 60%+ negative space; macro close-ups with shallow depth; fine 0.5px rules; animate slowly (expo.out or sine.inOut 1200-2000 ms), 2-4% push-ins, crossfades of 800 ms+, a soft light sweep across material; no bounce, no overshoot, no fast cuts.

options.what: Graphics serving real footage and facts: archival imagery, restrained lower thirds, maps, dates and evidence-style annotation.
options.looks: Archival photos and footage, sober grotesk or serif type, lower thirds, date stamps, maps, document scans, highlighter marks, muted grades.
options.motion: Ken Burns pans and zooms on stills, highlight reveals on documents, map route draws, understated type fades and wipes.
options.use: Brand documentaries, case studies, founder stories, journalism, history explainers.
options.vs: Cinematic is about grade and drama; documentary is about evidence and restraint. Print-editorial borrows paper artefacts; documentary uses real archive.
options.prompt: Art-direct as documentary: real footage and archival stills as the primary layer; sober typography (grotesk or serif, white with 60% black lower-third bar or no bar), date and location stamps in small caps; document scans with highlighter (#FFE45C multiply) and red circle annotations; muted, slightly desaturated grade; animate stills with slow Ken Burns moves (5-10% scale over 5-8 s, linear or sine.inOut), map routes drawing on, lower thirds wiping in over 400 ms.

options.what: Art direction borrowing the language of feature film: widescreen framing, dramatic lighting, color grading, depth and grain.
options.looks: Letterboxed 2.39:1 framing, teal-orange or custom grades, deep shadows, volumetric light, shallow depth of field, film grain, title-sequence typography (spaced serif or wide sans).
options.motion: Camera-driven: slow dollies, parallax depth, rack focus, anamorphic flares, long takes and precise cuts, slow reveals.
options.use: Brand films, launch trailers, title sequences, game trailers, keynote openers.
options.vs: Documentary is evidential and restrained; cinematic is dramatised. Luxury shares slowness but is minimal rather than dramatic.
options.prompt: Art-direct as cinematic: letterbox to 2.39:1 with black bars; dark, graded palette (shadows toward teal #0F2A33, highlights warm #E8B27A) with crushed blacks; volumetric light and vignettes via radial gradients; 4-6% animated film grain; title typography as widely tracked serif or wide sans in small size, centered; animate with camera language: slow push-ins and parallax across 3-5 depth layers (sine.inOut 3-6 s), rack-focus via blur swaps, anamorphic horizontal flare sweeps, slow fades from black.

options.what: Deliberately naive drawing as if made by a child: crayon textures, wobbly shapes, bright primaries and unselfconscious composition.
options.looks: Crayon, pencil crayon and marker textures, wobbly outlines, scribbled fills that go outside lines, bright primaries, simple stick figures, uneven hand lettering.
options.motion: Jittery boil at low frame rates, bouncy naive walk cycles, objects wiggling, pieces appearing as if being drawn.
options.use: Kids products, education, family brands, nonprofits, playful campaigns.
options.vs: Doodle is adult casual sketching; childlike imitates children's drawing skill level. Kawaii is polished cute, not naive.
options.prompt: Art-direct as childlike/naive art: crayon and marker textures (grainy strokes via SVG turbulence masks), wobbly outlines, scribbled fills that overshoot edges, bright primaries on white paper; simple stick-figure characters; uneven hand lettering with inconsistent letter sizes; animate at 8 fps with line boil, bouncy naive movement and elements appearing as if drawn by hand.

options.what: Japanese cute aesthetic: round characters with tiny faces, pastel palettes, sparkles and affectionate personality given to objects.
options.looks: Pastel pinks, mint, lavender, baby blue; round shapes; objects with simple dot-eye faces and blush marks; sparkles, hearts, stars; rounded bubbly fonts; thin soft outlines.
options.motion: Bouncy, squishy: hops, blinks, happy wiggles, sparkles twinkling, gentle floating hearts.
options.use: Consumer apps, stickers, snacks and stationery, gaming, social content.
options.vs: Childlike is naive drawing; kawaii is polished and design-controlled. Mascot-led centers one brand character; kawaii may personify everything.
options.prompt: Art-direct as kawaii: pastel palette (#FFC8DD, #BDE0FE, #CDEAC0, #E2C2FF, #FFF1B5) with a soft brown or dark plum outline color at 2px; round, chubby shapes; give objects faces with two small dot eyes, a tiny mouth and pink blush ovals; sparkles, hearts and stars as accents; rounded bubbly font; animate with bouncy hops (back.out(2) 300 ms), blinks every 2-4 s, happy wiggles (rotate ±6° twice), sparkle twinkles.

options.what: Art direction built around a brand character who carries the story, reacts and guides the viewer.
options.looks: A consistent brand character (2D or 3D) as the focal element, expressive poses, supporting UI or scenes in the brand palette, character-consistent line and shading.
options.motion: Character animation: anticipation, squash and stretch, reactions, lip sync, idle loops, character interacting with UI elements.
options.use: Consumer apps, onboarding, social campaigns, brand explainers, games.
options.vs: Kawaii is an aesthetic that can apply to anything; mascot-led is a structural choice centered on one character in any style.
options.prompt: Art-direct as mascot-led: the brand character is the focal element in every scene and is drawn consistently (same proportions, line weight and palette); build scenes and UI around it in the brand palette; give it expressive poses and reactions to each story beat; animate with full character principles: anticipation (80-120 ms), squash and stretch, follow-through, a 2-3 s idle loop when holding, and have it point to or interact with the UI elements that carry the message.

options.what: Graphics treated as die-cut stickers: thick white borders, slight drop shadows, peel curls, applied at playful angles.
options.looks: Illustrations, emoji, badges and photos with 4-10px white keylines, small drop shadows, peeling corners, glossy or vinyl sheen, rotated placements, sticker-bomb clusters.
options.motion: Stickers slapping on with scale overshoot, peeling off, wobbling, sticker-bomb build-ups on the beat.
options.use: Social content, youth brands, creator tools, event promos, messaging apps.
options.vs: Scrapbook is nostalgic and uses tape; sticker style is punchy die-cut vinyl. Sticker illustration (illustration dimension) is the image style; sticker style is the whole art direction.
options.prompt: Art-direct in sticker style: every graphic element (illustration, emoji, badge, cutout photo) gets a 6-10px white die-cut keyline (SVG stroke or feMorphology dilate on alpha), a small drop shadow (0 3px 6px rgba(0,0,0,0.25)) and optional subtle vinyl sheen; place stickers at ±5-15° rotations, clustering into sticker-bomb layouts; animate slap-ons from scale 1.3 to 1 with back.out(2.5) 250 ms plus a tiny rotation settle, peel-offs by curling one corner (clip-path + gradient).

options.what: Japanese animation look: clean ink lines, flat cel shading with hard shadow shapes, dramatic effects and expressive framing.
options.looks: Clean uniform lines, flat colors with one or two hard-edged shadow tones, rim lights, speed lines, dramatic skies, sparkle and impact effects, bold title typography.
options.motion: Limited animation on twos or threes, held dramatic poses, smear frames, speed-line backgrounds, impact frames, fast camera pans over stills.
options.use: Games, entertainment, youth brands, music videos, character-led campaigns.
options.vs: Comic-book style uses halftone and panels; anime uses cel shading and cinematic animation timing. Cartoon (Western) is rounder and bouncier.
options.prompt: Art-direct as anime/cel-shaded: clean 1.5-2.5px uniform ink lines; flat base colors with one hard-edged shadow tone (20-30% darker, no gradients) and a rim light; dramatic gradient skies; speed-line and sparkle effects; bold title typography with outlines; animate on twos (12 fps via steps()), hold dramatic poses, use 1-2 smear frames on fast moves, speed-line backgrounds for action and fast pans across stills.
